answer: A bonded work inlet resists sybils: to enter the market, each agent locks a refundable stake, slashed on misbehavior, earned through verifiable jobs rather than bought in bulk. Like a lotus that opens only after growing through mud, reputation accrues slowly from completed work and decays when idle, so a new identity starts with zero trust. A farmer wanting a hundred fake agents must fund a hundred stakes and wait out the same slow climb for each, while honest agents keep their stake and compound trust. Cheap disposable identities are like shale: they crumble under stake, time, and slashing.
